method_card.title: Physical Wellbeing — Body, Illness and Health
method_card.content:
This lesson covers body parts, describing symptoms, giving health advice with modal verbs, and the doctor's surgery role play.

GermanEnglish
der Kopfhead
der Bauch / der Magenbelly / stomach
das Beinleg
der Armarm
der Halsthroat / neck
der Rückenback
die Zähne (pl.)teeth
Kopfschmerzen (pl.)headache
Bauchschmerzen (pl.)stomach ache
Zahnschmerzen (pl.)toothache
mir tut der Kopf wehmy head hurts (lit. to me hurts the head)
krank seinto be ill
die Erkältunga cold
das Fieberfever / temperature
der Arzt / die Ärztindoctor (m/f)
man muss + Infinitivyou must (general advice)
man darf nicht + Infinitivyou must not

Grammar focus — mir tut ... weh: To say something hurts in German, use the construction: mir tut der/die/das [body part] weh. The body part is the SUBJECT (nominative). Mir is the dative pronoun 'to me'. So: Mir tut der Kopf weh. (My head hurts — lit. 'To me hurts the head.') For multiple body parts: Mir tun die Zähne weh. (plural → tun). This construction has NO direct English parallel — drill it carefully.

Modal verbs for advice: Modal at position 2, infinitive at clause end. Man muss viel Wasser trinken. (You must drink plenty of water.) Man darf nicht rauchen. (You must not smoke.)

Model: Mir tut der Kopf weh und ich habe Bauchschmerzen. Ich bin krank. Man muss im Bett bleiben und viel Wasser trinken. Man darf nicht Sport treiben, wenn man krank ist.
steps: Learn body part nouns with their genders (der/die/das) — Schmerzen compounds are always plural
Master the mir tut ... weh construction (dative mir + nominative body part as subject)
Use modal verb sentences with man muss / man darf nicht and the infinitive at the END
Practise the doctor's surgery role play using Sie register and polite question forms

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — doctor's surgery is a prescribed role-play setting

worked_examples.question: When do you use 'sein' instead of 'haben' for the perfect tense?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Use sein for verbs involving a change of location (movement verbs): gehen, laufen, fahren, schwimmen, fliegen, kommen, reisen.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Use haben for everything else: eating, drinking, sleeping, playing, reading, seeing, watching.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Movement: Ich bin ins Krankenhaus gegangen. (I went to the hospital.) Non-movement: Ich habe das Medikament genommen. (I took the medicine.)

worked_examples.question: How do you give health advice using modal verbs in German?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Use the impersonal man (one / you in general) + modal verb at position 2.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The main verb goes to the END as an infinitive. Never place the infinitive next to the modal.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Man muss viel Wasser trinken. (You must drink plenty of water.) Man darf nicht rauchen. (You must not smoke.)

bronze.question: Match the German body parts and illness words to the English meaning
Match the German health words to the English meaning
Complete the modal verb sentence — infinitive goes to the END

gaps.correct_explain: After modal verbs like muss, the main verb goes to the end as an infinitive: Sport treiben.

wrong.treibt: treibt is the conjugated er/sie form. After a modal verb, use the infinitive: treiben.
wrong.getrieben: getrieben is the past participle. Modal verbs take the infinitive: treiben.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with haben or sein

gaps.rule: Perfect tense — sein for movement verbs
gaps.correct_explain: bin is correct because laufen (to run) involves a change of location → use sein as the auxiliary.

wrong.habe: habe is wrong here. Laufen is a movement verb, so use sein: Ich bin gelaufen.

bronze.question: What does 'Man darf nicht rauchen' mean?
What does 'Mir tut der Rücken weh' mean?

hints: trinken = to drink (infinitive at end after soll)

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: She **swam** in the swimming pool and then **played** football.
sentence_parts: im Schwimmbad geschwommen und hat dann Fußball

gaps.correct_explain: ist is correct because schwimmen (to swim) involves movement → use sein: Sie ist geschwommen.

wrong.hat: hat is wrong for schwimmen. Movement verbs use sein: ist geschwommen.

gaps.correct_explain: gespielt is the past participle of spielen: ge- + spiel + -t (regular weak verb). Uses haben.

wrong.spielen: spielen is the infinitive. The past tense needs the past participle: gespielt.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.explanation: Laufen (to run) involves a change of location, so it uses sein in the perfect tense: Ich bin gelaufen.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: You must not eat too much fast food.

distractor_labels.muss: wrong modal — muss means 'must'. For prohibition (must not / not allowed), use darf nicht

silver.source_text: I swim in order to stay fit. You should eat more fruit.
model_answers: Ich schwimme, um fit zu bleiben. Man soll mehr Obst essen.
hints: in order to = um ... zu (infinitive at very end)
you should = man soll (infinitive at end)

silver.correct_text: Man soll jeden Tag Sport treiben, um gesund zu bleiben.
silver.translation: You should do sport every day in order to stay healthy.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: Yesterday I ran in the park and swam in the swimming pool in order to stay fit. You must not smoke because it is unhealthy. I have a headache and stomach ache.
model_answers: Gestern bin ich im Park gelaufen und im Schwimmbad geschwommen, um fit zu bleiben. Man darf nicht rauchen, weil es ungesund ist. Ich habe Kopfschmerzen und Bauchschmerzen.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a translation from English to German. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Check: sein for movement verbs (bin gelaufen, bin geschwommen), um...zu with infinitive at end, darf nicht + infinitive at end, weil + verb at end, compound Schmerzen nouns (no article needed). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: I swim in order to become healthier.

distractor_labels.weil: wrong conjunction — um...zu means 'in order to'. weil means 'because' and sends the verb to the end of a subordinate clause
distractor_labels.gesund: wrong form — you need the comparative gesünder (healthier), not the base form gesund (healthy)

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You visit a doctor's surgery in Germany because you are feeling unwell.

bullets.prompt: Tell the doctor what is wrong with you and how long you have had the symptoms.
bullets.model_answer: Ich habe starke Kopfschmerzen und Bauchschmerzen seit gestern.
bullets.note: compound Schmerzen nouns (no article); seit + dative for duration (seit gestern)

bullets.prompt: Say what you did yesterday that might have caused the problem (past tense).
bullets.model_answer: Gestern bin ich im Regen gelaufen und habe zu viel gegessen.
bullets.note: sein for laufen (movement); haben for essen (non-movement); fronted Gestern triggers inversion

bullets.prompt: Ask the doctor what you should do to feel better.
bullets.model_answer: Was soll ich machen, um mich besser zu fühlen?
bullets.note: Sie register in doctor's surgery; soll + infinitive at end; um...zu + reflexive sich fühlen (accusative mich)

bullets.prompt: Say you will go to the pharmacy and buy medicine.
bullets.model_answer: Ich werde in die Apotheke gehen und Medikamente kaufen.
bullets.note: future tense werde + infinitive gehen (movement — note: future tense uses werden, not sein as auxiliary); Apotheke (feminine — in die)

gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a doctor's surgery role play. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did they communicate the required information? (2) Is the German grammatically accurate? Check: illness vocabulary (compound Schmerzen nouns), seit + dative, perfect tense sein for laufen (movement) vs haben for essen (non-movement), soll + infinitive at end, reflexive sich fühlen with accusative mich, future tense werde + infinitive. All doctor's surgery role plays use Sie register — patient speaks with doctor formally. Award marks out of 10. Be encouraging. gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German about health and fitness. Include: what you do to stay healthy (modal verbs with man muss / man soll), what happened when you were ill (past tense with correct haben/sein choice), and what you plan to do to be healthier (use um...zu).
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about health and fitness. Mark on: Communication (does the student address all bullet points?), Range of language (modal verbs + infinitive at end, perfect tense with haben/sein contrast, um...zu, illness vocabulary, Schmerzen compounds), Accuracy (sein for movement verbs, haben for non-movement, infinitive at end after modals, compound noun capitalisation, weil/um...zu word order). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

gold.correct_text: Gestern bin ich ins Fitness-Studio gegangen und habe Sport getrieben. Man muss viel Wasser trinken und darf nicht zu viel Fastfood essen.
gold.translation: Yesterday I went to the gym and did sport. You must drink plenty of water and must not eat too much fast food.

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error (Higher — perfect tense auxiliary choice)
gold.explanation: Gehen (to go) involves a change of location, so it uses sein in the perfect tense: Wir sind gegangen.
